key_insight: WorldSolver shows that LLM agents can sometimes generate physical simulation solvers, but achieving executable, visually accurate, and physically plausible dynamics remains very challenging.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark targets a practical gap in scientific and graphics software: using LLM agents to automatically implement simulation code for dynamic physical systems.
method: Built 168 simulation tasks from 61 classic computer graphics papers across 7 physical domains
Each task includes a fixed code scaffold; the agent must complete the solver implementation
Evaluated outputs on execution success, visual fidelity, and physical plausibility
evidence_signal: Across frontier agents, GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude-Opus-5 were the strongest, but their overall scores were still only 48.7% and 46.7%, showing solver generation is far from solved.
watch_item: A solver that executes correctly may still produce unrealistic or physically incorrect dynamics, so visual and physics-based checks are necessary.
paper_title: WorldSolver: Can LLM Agents Simulate the Physical Dynamics via Solver Generation?
